title: WCAG 2.3.3 motion animation and reduce-motion settings
statement:
WCAG 2.3.3 (Level AAA) says motion animation triggered by interaction, such as parallax scrolling, should be possible to disable because scroll-triggered movement can trigger vestibular disorders with dizziness, nausea and headaches, and honoring the operating system's reduce-motion setting is the standard route.

Options:
- Reduced-motion media query: Parallax and large transforms wrapped in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) so they are off for users who request reduced motion (fits: modern, technical, polished)
- Fade instead of move: Opacity-only fades or static reveals instead of translation and parallax effects (fits: calm, minimal, premium)
- Motion toggle: On-page 'reduce motion' toggle that disables non-essential animation site-wide (fits: accessible, respectful, careful)
- Subtle micro-interactions only: Short, subtle micro-interactions (button states, hovers) kept separate from large scroll-linked effects (fits: professional, efficient, trustworthy)
appliesWhen: Applies to: general web. Audience: general.

source.title: Understanding SC 2.3.3: Animation from Interactions, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1
source.venue: W3C WCAG 2.2 (SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions, Level AAA, introduced in WCAG 2.1 in 2018)
